Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The unemployment rate is 4.9% and the fed funds rate is 0.40%, which points to 2016. The 10-year yield is 1.52%, down 0.31 over three months, and gold is up 23.7% over 12 months, so mid-to-late 2016 fits. The 10y-2y spread is 0.80.

Several details help narrow the month:
- Fed funds near 0.40% fits the period before the December 2016 hike, when the rate was about 0.37–0.40%.
- The 10-year at 1.52% fits August or September 2016. In July 2016 it was about 1.46%, and in August about 1.58%.
- Unemployment was 4.9% in both August and September 2016.
- Headline CPI at 1.05% year over year fits July 2016 (0.8%) or August (1.1%).
- Core CPI at 2.23% fits August 2016 (2.3%).
- The 3-month payroll average of 147k fits August 2016 (about 120k after revisions) or perhaps July.
- The 1-month equity gain of 5.1%, led by emerging markets at +6.4% and developed ex-US at +5.5%, fits July 2016 better than August, when the monthly gain was about 0.1%. July 2016 was the S&P's strong month at about +3.7%, so 5.1% is a bit high.
- Another candidate is a month where the 3-month change in the 10-year is -0.31. From 1.81 at the end of April 2016 to 1.50 at the end of July matches that.
- The 12-month return on developed ex-US of -7.2% also fits July 2016.

The 12-month change in the dollar of -11.31 looks odd, but it is probably a data quirk. I'll pick July 2016 over August.
